target_moa.text: Etelcalcetide is a calcimimetic (calcium-sensing receptor agonist) that allosterically modulates the CaSR on parathyroid chief cells, enhancing activation by extracellular calcium and thereby decreasing PTH secretion.

citations.quote: Etelcalcetide is a calcimimetic agent that allosterically modulates the calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR). Etelcalcetide binds to the CaSR and enhances activation of the receptor by extracellular calcium. Activation of the CaSR on parathyroid chief cells decreases PTH secretion.
PARSABIV (etelcalcetide) is a synthetic peptide calcium-sensing receptor agonist.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) were blood calcium decreased (64% vs 10% placebo), muscle spasms (12% vs 7%), diarrhea (11% vs 9%), nausea (11% vs 6%), vomiting (9% vs 5%), headache (8% vs 6%), hypocalcemia (7% vs 0.2%), and paresthesia (6% vs 1%). Key warnings: hypocalcemia (sometimes severe, with QT prolongation risk), worsening heart failure, upper GI bleeding, and adynamic bone.

summary.text: Parsabiv (etelcalcetide) received traditional (Standard-review) approval on the NDA received August 24, 2015; efficacy was established in two adequate and well-controlled placebo-controlled trials using PTH reduction as an accepted surrogate. FDA first issued a Complete Response (August 24, 2016) over the sponsor's superiority-vs-cinacalcet claim, and the drug was approved after a December 9, 2016 resubmission. No advisory committee was convened.
